# HeatOS: Lansing data center heat reuse

*Generated 2026-10-03 20:07 from the live HeatOS model.*
*Pitch: Data center heat that neighbors can count on, with a price for that certainty.*

> **Data status.** Data providers: buildings: mock, weather: mock, demand: mock, supply: mock, confidence: mock, jev: OpenJev (jev-latest)
> Every number below is computed by the model; the source of each input is listed in Appendix A. Inputs marked "assumption - verify" are placeholders to be confirmed.

---

## 1. Decision framework: where heat reuse should go first

HeatOS scores both candidate sites on nine weighted criteria (1-5 scale).

| Criterion | Weight | Chelsea | Lansing | Why |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Demand density | 10% | 5 | 2 | dense multi-family and commercial blocks vs dispersed rural users |
| Source temperature | 10% | 3 | 5 | air-cooled 27-32 C vs liquid-cooled 45-65 C |
| Supply continuity | 10% | 3 | 3 | colocation tenants vs crypto-exposed flexible load |
| Cost of heat displaced | 10% | 5 | 4 | Con Ed steam and oil vs propane and oil |
| Infrastructure cost per MWh | 15% | 3 | 3 | street works in Manhattan vs long rural runs |
| Carbon displaced | 10% | 4 | 4 | steam/gas on a 0.25-0.44 t/MWh grid vs propane/oil on a cleaner grid |
| Local air / water / noise | 10% | 5 | 3 | PM2.5 92nd percentile block vs clean rural air |
| Vulnerable people served | 15% | 5 | 2 | public housing towers next door vs no disadvantaged communities |
| Community acceptance leverage | 10% | 3 | 5 | heat as a host-community benefit for a contested data center |
| **Weighted total** | 100% | **4.00** | **3.35** | |

**Robustness.** Across 100,000 random re-weightings (Dirichlet, alpha = weight x 40) with +/-0.75 noise on every score, **Chelsea ranks first in 96.6% of draws**. Recommendation: **Chelsea**.

Within the chosen site, a building connects only if its best option has a positive 20-year value (financial NPV at 6% plus avoided CO2 at $190/t), and only while the data center has firm capacity left. Buildings are added in priority order: NPV x (1 + equity score) x boiler urgency.

## 2. Data analysis

### Datasets and models
| Component | Method | Datasets | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mock building inventory | hand-placed archetypes; heat = floor area x use-type intensity | synthetic | MOCK (teammate model pending) |
| Mock weather | seasonal sinusoid + diurnal + AR(1) noise | synthetic (NYC / Ithaca climate normals, approximate) | MOCK (teammate model pending) |
| Mock demand model | degree-day (base 18 C) space heat + hot-water daily profile, calibrated to annual totals | mock building inventory, mock weather | MOCK (teammate model pending) |
| Mock supply model | capacity x capture fraction x daily load factor (0.75-0.95) + noise | site config | MOCK (teammate model pending) |
| Mock confidence engine | 100 futures, uniform jitter, engine simulator | engine simulator outputs | MOCK (teammate model pending) |
| OpenJev (jev-latest) | typed System One decisions read from model probabilities | live network state rendered as text | v0.5 |


### Building inventory (25 candidates)
| Heating system | Buildings | Annual heat (MWh) |
|---|---:|---:|
| electric | 1 | 726 |
| oil | 6 | 8,349 |
| propane | 18 | 31,868 |


### Recommendation (17 buildings connected)
| Building | Use | Option | Phase | 20-yr value NPV | Reasons |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Greenhouse 5 | greenhouse | direct use | 1 | $7,546,681 |  |
| Greenhouse 6 | greenhouse | direct use | 1 | $7,541,909 |  |
| Greenhouse 4 | greenhouse | direct use | 1 | $7,394,897 |  |
| Greenhouse 2 | greenhouse | direct use | 1 | $7,028,059 |  |
| Greenhouse 3 | greenhouse | direct use | 1 | $6,904,079 |  |
| Middle school | school | direct use | 1 | $4,633,966 | boiler urgent |
| Greenhouse 1 | greenhouse | direct use | 2 | $6,723,898 |  |
| Aquaculture hall A | aquaculture | direct use | 2 | $3,210,096 |  |
| Aquaculture hall B | aquaculture | direct use | 2 | $3,072,212 |  |
| High school | school | direct use | 2 | $792,986 | boiler urgent, carbon value tips npv |
| Elementary school | school | direct use | 2 | $782,666 | boiler urgent |
| Village homes V1 (32 homes) | home | booster | 2 | $584,686 | boiler urgent |
| Ridge homes (26 homes) | home | booster | 3 | $503,020 |  |
| Hamlet homes E3 (40 homes) | home | booster | 3 | $485,102 | carbon value tips npv |
| Community center | school | direct use | 3 | $362,533 | boiler urgent |
| Senior cottages (16 homes) | home | booster | 3 | $233,317 | high equity |
| Village homes V2 (20 homes) | home | booster | 3 | $205,488 | boiler urgent, carbon value tips npv |


Not connected: 8 buildings with no option of positive value; 0 worthwhile buildings waiting on capacity. Firm capacity used: 10,312 of 12,282 kW.

### Key modelling assumptions
- Heat pump COP = eta x T_hot / (T_hot - T_cold), eta 0.6 (range 0.5-0.8).
- Energy balance closes every simulated hour within 0.1%; a full year simulates in under a second.
- Autopilot: rules (data center heat, then storage, then existing boilers) or MPC (48 h linear program minimizing electricity + fuel + carbon).
- Full parameter list with sources: Appendix A.

## 3. Sustainability impact (full simulated year)

| Metric | Central | Range |
|---|---:|---|
| Heat delivered | 35,412 MWh | |
| Fuel displaced | 41,828 MWh | electric: 717.5, oil: 8295.9, propane: 32814.4 |
| Net CO2 avoided | 10,154 t/yr | 9,841-10,780 (grid factor range) |
| Per MW thermal-year | 508 t | sanity band at this utilization 415-541: pass |
| Energy Reuse Factor (ERF) | 0.2275 | reused / IT energy |
| Energy Reuse Effectiveness (ERE) | 0.9225 | (facility - reused) / IT energy |


### HDR regenerative scorecard (-2 degenerative ... +2 regenerative)
| Category | Baseline | With HeatOS | Baseline basis | Change basis |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Community | 0 | 1 | no disadvantaged communities nearby (HDR site packet) | 4 guaranteed public facilities (schools / community center) |
| Human Health | 0 | 1 | rural; no acute exposure flagged | 100% of connected buildings' heat no longer burned on site |
| Air | 1 | 2 | clean air (HDR site packet) | 100% of connected buildings' heat no longer burned on site |
| Carbon | -1 | 2 | propane / oil heating; large new data center load | net CO2 avoided = 110% of connected buildings' existing heating emissions (incl. avoided data center cooling) |
| Water | 0 | 0 | lake-adjacent; liquid cooling, no towers | no material change modelled |
| Nutrients | -1 | 0 | Cayuga Lake phosphorus-impaired (HDR site packet) | greenhouse + aquaculture nutrient recovery assumed (assumption - verify) |
| Biodiversity | -1 | 0 | former coal plant and coal yard (brownfield) | pit storage on the remediated coal yard (assumption - verify) |


## 4. Risk assessment

| Risk | Type | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Owner | Linked stress test | Modelled result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lake-effect cold snap | Climate / technical | Medium | Medium | Pit storage sized for seasonal shifting; boilers kept at each user | Joint venture | lake effect cold snap | backup +0 MWh/week vs normal; storage used 45 MWh; guaranteed missed hours 0 |
| Crypto price crash switches off flexible load | Market | High | Medium | Heat contracts on the firm (non-flexible) share; pit storage bridges | TeraWulf | bitcoin price crash | backup +0 MWh/week vs normal; storage used 7 MWh; guaranteed missed hours 0 |
| Greenhouse operator off-season or exit | Commercial | Medium | Medium | Pit absorbs surplus; schools and homes phase in | Joint venture | greenhouse off season | backup -0 MWh/week vs normal; storage used 0 MWh; guaranteed missed hours 0 |
| Data center outage | Technical | Low | Low | Pit storage ride-through | TeraWulf | server outage | backup +0 MWh/week vs normal; storage used 40 MWh; guaranteed missed hours 0 |
| Electricity price spike | Market | Medium | Low | Mostly direct use; only boosters use power | Homes co-op | price spike | backup +0 MWh/week vs normal; storage used 0 MWh; guaranteed missed hours 0 |
| Community opposition to the data center | Social | Medium | High | Heat as a host-community benefit; tax abatement tied to heat delivery | Town of Lansing | - | - |
| Cayuga Lake nutrient / thermal impacts | Environmental | Low | High | Closed loops; aquaculture effluent treated; monitoring (verify) | Joint venture | - | - |


**Confidence.** Over the next 48 h, P(all connected buildings fully served by the network) = 100%; expected hours on backup 0.0; top uncertainty drivers: Building heat demand 81%, Electricity price 19%, Heat pump efficiency 0% (40 futures, mock_uniform_jitter).

## 5. Implementation vision

### Phase 1: Built-in from day one
TeraWulf's liquid cooling exports 45-65 C water through a heat export station.
Buildings: Greenhouse 2, Greenhouse 3, Greenhouse 4, Greenhouse 5, Greenhouse 6, Middle school.

### Phase 2: Greenhouse park and pit storage
Greenhouses, aquaculture and schools take warm water directly; the pit on the remediated coal yard shifts summer surplus to winter.
Buildings: Greenhouse 1, Aquaculture hall A, Aquaculture hall B, High school, Elementary school, Village homes V1 (32 homes).

### Phase 3: Homes co-op
Home clusters along the loop join a co-op; small booster heat pumps make hot tap water, financed on the bill.
Buildings: Community center, Hamlet homes E3 (40 homes), Ridge homes (26 homes), Village homes V2 (20 homes), Senior cottages (16 homes).

### Who pays, and does everyone come out ahead?
| Party | Upfront | Financed | Annual operating | 20-yr NPV | Payback | P(ahead) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TeraWulf (data center) | $7,180,656 | $0 | $3,335,478 | $31,077,019 | 3 | 100% |
| Joint venture (TeraWulf + Town of Lansing / Tompkins County) | $14,888,198 | $0 | $2,229,163 | $10,680,123 | 7 | 100% |
| Greenhouses, aquaculture and schools | $0 | $0 | $954,594 | $10,949,112 | 0 | 100% |
| Homes co-op | $0 | $177,912 | $60,073 | $522,558 | 0 | 100% |


**Everyone wins?** Yes: every party is ahead in at least 80% of 16 sampled futures with the configured terms.

## Appendix B: how each headline number is computed
- **Site scores**: engine/site_scoring.py: weights and scores in CRITERIA; robustness = 100,000 Dirichlet draws
- **Recommendation**: engine/recommend.py: per-option 20-yr NPV at the site discount rate + avoided CO2 x carbon price
- **Heat, backup, electricity**: engine/physics.py + engine/sim.py: hourly simulation with energy balance checked every hour
- **Net CO2**: engine/impact.py: fuel displaced x fuel factor - (heat pump + pump electricity) x grid + chiller electricity avoided x grid
- **Water**: engine/impact.py: evaporation = heat (MJ) / 2.26; tower water = evaporation / 0.67; minus 2 gal per kWh of added electricity
- **Party economics**: engine/ledger.py: hourly money flows, capex by party (pipe = minimum spanning tree), NPV at each party's rate
- **Everyone wins / guarantee premiums**: engine/guarantees.py: sampled futures through the simulator; premium = E[refunds] + CVaR95 margin
- **Stress-test results**: engine/scenarios.py: 7-day runs from 12 Jan (heat wave: 10 Jul), stress fired at hour 24, rules autopilot
